name: Fast Friends
text:
When you need to make sure something gets done, you can't rely on vague promises, sworn oaths, or binding contracts of employment. When you cast this spell, choose one humanoid within range that can see and hear you, and that can understand you. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become {@condition charmed} by you for the duration. While the creature is {@condition charmed} in this way, it undertakes to perform any services or activities you ask of it in a friendly manner, to the best of its ability.
You can set the creature new tasks when a previous task is completed, or if you decide to end its current task. If the service or activity might cause harm to the creature, or if it conflicts with the creature's normal activities and desires, the creature can make another Wisdom saving throw to try to end the effect. This save is made with advantage if you or your companions are fighting the creature. If the activity would result in certain death for the creature, the spell ends.
When the spell ends, the creature knows it was {@condition charmed} by you.
higher:
At Higher Levels
When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 3rd.

name: Gift of Gab

time.condition: which you take when you speak to another creature

text:
When I met Jim Darkmagic, I wondered how he got anything done in that outfit. I have since learned that most of his talents involve standing and talking. His outfit is perfect for that.
Jim Darkmagic is said to have invented this spell, originally calling it {@i I said what?!} Have you ever been talking to the local monarch and accidentally mentioned how their son looks like your favorite hog from when you were growing up on the family farm? We've all been there! But rather than being beheaded for an honest slip of the tongue, you can pretend it never happened—by ensuring that no one knows it happened.
When you cast this spell, you skillfully reshape the memories of listeners in your immediate area, so that each creature of your choice within 5 feet of you forgets everything you said within the last 6 seconds. Those creatures then remember that you actually said the words you speak as the verbal component of the spell.

name: Incite Greed

m.text: a gem worth at least 50 gp

text:
When you cast this spell, you present the gem used as the material component and choose any number of creatures within range that can see you. Each target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition charmed} by you until the spell ends, or until you or your companions do anything harmful to it. While {@condition charmed} in this way, a creature can do nothing but use its movement to approach you in a safe manner. While an affected creature is within 5 feet of you, it cannot move, but simply stares greedily at the gem you present.
At the end of each of its turns, an affected target can make a Wisdom saving throw. If it succeeds, this effect ends for that target.

name: Jim's Glowing Coin
text: Of the many tactics employed by master magician and renowned adventurer Jim Darkmagic, the old glowing coin trick is a time-honored classic. When you cast the spell, you hurl the coin that is the spell's material component to any spot within range. The coin lights up as if under the effect of a {@spell light} spell. Each creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of the coin must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be distracted for the duration. While distracted, a creature has disadvantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks and initiative rolls.

name: Jim's Magic Missile
text:
Jim's magic missile is an ancient and powerful spell, as well as being the name of my band in Wizard Academy.
Any apprentice wizard can cast a boring old magic missile. Sure, it always strikes its target. Yawn. Do away with the drudgery of your grandfather's magic with this improved version of the spell, as used by Jim Darkmagic!
You create three twisting, whistling, hypoallergenic, gluten-free darts of magical force. Each dart targets a creature of your choice that you can see within range. Make a ranged spell attack for each missile. On a hit, a missile deals {@damage 2d4} force damage to its target.
If the attack roll scores a critical hit, the target of that missile takes {@damage 5d4} force damage instead of you rolling damage twice for a critical hit. If the attack roll for any missile is a 1, all missiles miss their targets and blow up in your face, dealing 1 force damage per missile to you.
higher:
At Higher Levels
When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the spell creates one more dart, and the royalty component increases by 1 gp, for each slot level above 1st.

name: Motivational Speech
text:
I once heard a motivational speech by Jim and it was the worst ninety seconds of my life. What does Omin see in him, anyway?
You address allies, staff, or innocent bystanders to exhort and inspire them to greatness, whether they have anything to get excited about or not. Choose up to five creatures within range that can hear you. For the duration, each affected creature gains 5 temporary hit points and has advantage on Wisdom saving throws. If an affected creature is hit by an attack, it has advantage on the next attack roll it makes. Once an affected creature loses the temporary hit points granted by this spell, the spell ends for that creature.
higher:
At Higher Levels
When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the temporary hit points increase by 5 for each slot level above 3rd.

name: Linked Glyphs

m.text: incense and powdered diamond worth at least 300 gp, which the spell consumes

text:
When you cast this spell, you inscribe a detection glyph that later activates a magical effect at the site of a separate, linked glyph. You inscribe the detection glyph either on a surface (such as a table or a section of floor or wall) or within an object that can be closed (such as a book, a scroll, or a treasure chest) to conceal the glyph. The glyph can cover an area no larger than 10 feet in diameter. If the surface or object is moved more than 10 feet from where you cast this spell, the detection glyph is broken, and the spell ends without being triggered.
Both glyphs are nearly invisible, and finding either requires a successful Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check against your spell save DC.
You decide what triggers the detection glyph when you cast this spell. For glyphs inscribed on a surface, the most typical triggers include touching or standing on the glyph, removing another object covering the glyph, approaching within a certain distance of the glyph, or manipulating the object on which the glyph is inscribed. For glyphs inscribed within an object, the most common triggers include opening that object, approaching within a certain distance of the object, or seeing or reading the glyph. Once a glyph is triggered, this spell ends.
You can further refine the trigger so the spell activates only under certain circumstances or according to physical characteristics (such as height or weight), creature kind (for example, the ward could be set to affect aberrations or drow), or alignment. You can also set conditions for creatures that don't trigger the glyph, such as those who say a certain password.
When you inscribe the detection glyph, choose an alarm glyph or spell glyph to link to it.
Alarm Glyph
You create and magically link two glyphs: a detection glyph and an effect glyph. Each of these two glyphs must stay within 100 miles of the other or the spell effect ends. When the detection glyph is triggered, the effect glyph reacts like an alarm spell, creating a mental ping in your mind if you are within 1 mile of the effect glyph. This ping awakens you if you are sleeping.
Spell Glyph
You create and magically link two glyphs: a detection glyph and an effect glyph. These two glyphs must be within 100 feet of each other. You can store a prepared spell of 4th level or lower in the effect glyph by casting it as part of creating the glyphs. The spell must target a single creature or an area. The spell being stored has no immediate effect when cast in this way. When the detection glyph is triggered, the spell stored in the effect glyph is cast. If the spell has a target, it targets the creature that triggered the glyph. If the spell affects an area, the area is centered on the effect glyph. If the spell summons hostile creatures or creates harmful objects or traps, they appear as close as possible to the effect glyph. If the spell requires {@status concentration}, it lasts until the end of its full duration.
higher:
At Higher Levels
When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher to create a spell glyph, you can store any spell of up to the same level as the slot you use.

name: Aura of Evasion
text: An aura of alacrity radiates from you in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} for the duration. While in the aura, you and your allies have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity saving throws. When an affected creature is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, it takes no damage if it succeeds on the save and only half damage if it fails. A creature with the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition doesn't gain any benefit from being in the aura.

name: Catnap
text: You make a calming gesture, and up to three willing creatures of your choice that you can see within range have the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition for the spell's duration. The spell ends on a target if it takes damage or another creature takes an action to shake it awake. If a target has the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition from this spell for the full duration, that target gains the benefits of finishing a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and it can't be affected by this spell again until it finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
higher:
Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
You can target one additional willing creature for each spell slot level above 3.

name: Detonate
text:
You create a magical, explosive seed inside a creature you can see within range. The target makes a Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 10d10} Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.
An explosion then originates from the target. Each creature in a 60-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the target (not including the target) makes a Dexterity saving throw, with {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} if this spell reduced the target to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. A creature takes {@damage 10d10} Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.
A nonmagical object that isn't being worn or carried also takes the damage if it's in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}, and the object starts {@hazard burning|XPHB} if it's flammable.

name: Disruptive Tune
text: A distracting melody momentarily fills a 20-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on a point you choose within range. Each creature in the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target loses {@status Concentration|XPHB}, and it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} for the spell's duration.

name: Distorted Distance
text:
You create an illusory spatial dilation that fills a 60-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on a point within range. For each creature you can see in the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere}, you can choose one of the following effects for it:
Dizzying Elongation
The creature makes an Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 2d10} Psychic damage, and the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} for it until the end of its turn.
Shortened Space
The creature's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 20 feet until the end of its next turn.
Until the spell ends, whenever a creature enters the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} or ends its turn there, you can choose for it to receive one of these effects. A creature can be affected by this spell only once per turn.

name: Dueling Ground
text:
You create a magical dueling ground bounded by a glowing, rune-scribed circle in a 15-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on a point on the ground you touch.
As part of creating the dueling ground, you designate two willing creatures within the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} as the targets. The spell ends early if a creature other than one of the targets enters the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere}.
If a target drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} while in the dueling ground, the target is {@variantrule Stable|XPHB} and teleports to the nearest unoccupied space outside the dueling ground. If a target is subjected to an effect that would kill it instantly without dealing damage while in the dueling ground, the target doesn't die and instead has 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition, is {@variantrule Stable|XPHB}, and teleports to the nearest unoccupied space outside the dueling ground.
When only one target remains in the dueling ground, runes matching those on the ground around the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} briefly flash around the remaining target's head like a crown.
higher:
Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
You can target one additional willing creature for each spell slot level above 2.

name: Enervation
text:
A tendril of inky darkness reaches out from you to drain life from a creature you can see within range.
The target makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes {@damage 6d8} Necrotic damage. On each of your subsequent turns, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to deal {@damage 2d8} Necrotic damage to the target automatically. The spell ends if the target is ever outside the spell's range or it has {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} from you.
On a successful save, the target takes half the initial damage only, and the spell ends.
Whenever this spell deals damage to a target, you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half the amount of Necrotic damage dealt.
higher:
Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
The initial damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each spell slot level above 5.

name: Entrancing Mirrors
text:
You create dozens of illusory mirrors to confuse up to three creatures of your choice that you can see within range.
Each target makes an Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes {@damage 7d6} Psychic damage and has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition. While the target is {@condition Stunned|XPHB}, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only.
A {@condition Stunned|XPHB} target repeats the Intelligence saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the spell on itself on a success.

name: Festering Blast
text:
A 60-foot-long, 10-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} of miasma blasts from you in a direction you choose. Each creature in the {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes {@damage 4d10} Necrotic damage and has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for the duration.
A creature {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} by this spell takes {@damage 2d10} Poison damage at the start of each of its turns. At the end of each of its turns, a {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} target repeats the save, ending the spell on itself on a success.
higher:
Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
The initial damage increases by {@dice 1d10} for each spell slot level above 4.

name: Fractured Awareness
text:
You cause a creature to receive conflicting visions of multiple possible futures. Choose a creature you can see within range. The target makes an Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes {@damage 12d10} Psychic damage and has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests} for the duration. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage only, and the spell ends.
At the end of each of its turns, an affected target repeats the save, ending the spell on a success.

name: Grave Ground
text:
Skeletal hands burst from an area on the ground within range. The area consists of up to four 10-foot squares, which you arrange as you like. Each square must be contiguous with at least one other square. That area is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} for your enemies.
Any enemy in that area when the skeletal hands appear makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 6d6} Necrotic damage, and until the end of its next turn, the creature subtracts {@dice 1d6} from all its damage rolls. An enemy also makes this save if it enters the area or ends its turn there. A creature makes this save only once per turn.
higher:
Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
The damage increases by {@dice 1d6} for each spell slot level above 5.

name: Illusory Dragon
text:
By gathering threads of shadow material from the Shadowfell, you create a Huge shadowy dragon in an unoccupied space that you can see within range. The illusion lasts for the spell's duration and occupies its space as if it were a creature. The illusion is tangible because of the shadow material used to create it but has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to all damage and conditions.
When the illusion appears, any enemy that can see it makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature drops whatever it's holding and has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for the duration. If a creature {@condition Frightened|XPHB} in this way ends its turn in a space where it doesn't have line of sight to the illusion, the creature repeats the saving throw, ending the condition on itself on a success.
As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can move the illusion up to 60 feet. At any point during its movement, you can cause the shadowy dragon to exhale a blast of energy in a 60-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. Each creature in the {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} makes an Intelligence saving throw, taking {@damage 6d6} Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, or Poison damage (your choice when you create the dragon) on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.
A creature that takes a {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the dragon can determine that it is an illusion with a successful Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check against your spell save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the creature can see through the image and has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to end the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition it caused and to resist its exhalation.

name: Inflict Doubt
text: You inflict self-doubt on a creature you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests} for the duration. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the spell on itself on a success.

name: Iron Body

m.text: diamond dust worth 250+ GP, which the spell consumes

text: One willing creature you touch transforms into living metal. Until the spell ends, the target's {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level can't increase; the target has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Fire, Piercing, and Slashing damage; and it has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison damage and the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, {@condition Petrified|XPHB}, and {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} conditions. If the target is {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, {@condition Petrified|XPHB}, or {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} when you cast the spell, those conditions immediately end for the target.

name: Lightning Ring

components.m: a bit of fur and a glass ring

text:
A ring of crackling electricity fills a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you. Whenever the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} enters a creature's space and whenever a creature enters the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} or ends its turn there, you can force that creature to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 3d6} Lightning damage plus {@damage 3d6} Thunder damage, and it has the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage only.
As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action while the spell is active, you can emit a 60-foot-long, 5-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} out from you in a direction you choose. Each creature in the {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 6d6} Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

name: Negative Energy Flood

components.m: a broken bone and a square of black silk

text:
You send ribbons of negative energy at one creature you can see within range. If the target isn't Undead, it makes a Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 3d10 + 25} Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. A Humanoid killed by this spell rises at the start of your next turn as a {@creature Zombie|XMM} that follows your verbal orders for 24 hours, after which it acts according to its nature.
If the target is Undead, it gains {@dice 3d10} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.
higher:
Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
The damage increases by {@dice 1d10} for each spell slot level above 5.

name: Power Word Pain
text:
You speak a word of power that causes waves of intense pain to assail one creature you can see within range. If the target has 100 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or fewer, it takes {@damage 6d8} Force damage and has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition for the duration. Otherwise, it takes {@damage 6d8} Force damage only.
While the target is {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} can be no more than 10 feet, and it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests} except Constitution saving throws. In addition, when the target tries to cast a spell, it must first succeed on a Constitution saving throw, or the spell dissipates with no effect, and the action, {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, or {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} used to cast it is wasted. If that spell was cast with a spell slot, the slot isn't expended.
At the end of each of its turns, the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} target makes a Constitution saving throw, ending the spell on itself on a successful save.

name: Reweave Fate

time.condition: which you take when a creature you can see within 60 feet of you fails a D20 Test

text: You untangle a single thread of fate to encourage a different result. The creature that failed the {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} can reroll it with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}, and the creature must use the new roll. If the {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} is successful, the creature gains {@dice 6d10} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} from its strengthened fate.

name: Spirit Lantern
text:
You conjure a floating, ghostly black lantern that hovers above you and sheds {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} in a 60-foot radius. When an enemy dies within this {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB}, a fragment of the creature's soul flies into the lantern. The lantern can hold a number of soul fragments equal to your spellcasting ability modifier, and those fragments dissipate when the spell ends.
As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend a soul fragment to create one of the following effects.
Drain Life
The soul fragment darts at a creature of your choice that you can see within 60 feet of yourself. The target makes a Constitution saving throw, taking Necrotic damage equal to {@damage 4d8} plus your spellcasting ability modifier on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.
Repair Undead
The soul fragment flies into an Undead creature of your choice that you can see within 60 feet of yourself. That creature regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 4d8} plus your spellcasting ability modifier.
Ward Ally
The soul fragment darts around a creature of your choice that you can see within 60 feet of yourself. Other creatures have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against the chosen creature until the start of your next turn.

name: Transfix
text:
For the duration, your appearance becomes otherworldly and alluring. One creature of your choice that you can see within 60 feet of you must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or have the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition for the duration.
While {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, and if the target is more than 5 feet away from you, it moves on its turn toward you by the most direct route, trying to get within 5 feet of you. If the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} creature ends its turn within 5 feet of you, it takes {@damage 4d8} Psychic damage.
The target doesn't avoid {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} when moving toward you, but before moving into damaging terrain (such as lava or a pit), the target repeats the save, ending the spell on itself on a success.
Until the spell ends, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action on subsequent turns to target another creature, but you can't target a creature again if it has succeeded on a save against this casting of the spell.
higher:
Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
The damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each spell slot level above 7.

name: Uncertain Footing
text: You create illusory obstacles such as rocks or spikes in an attempt to confuse up to three creatures you can see within range, affecting their ability to move. Each target makes an Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, a target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved, and it can't take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action. A hampered target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the spell on itself on a success.

name: Vision of Elapsing Eons
text:
You trick a creature you can see within range into believing it is watching itself and its surroundings crumble away, as if eons were passing in moments. The target must succeed on an Intelligence saving throw or take {@damage 10d12} Psychic damage and have the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition for the duration.
While {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, the target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns. On a failed save, it gains 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level. On a successful save, the spell ends. The spell ends early if someone within 5 feet of the target takes an action to shake it free from the illusion.

name: Wail of the Banshee
text: You emit a terrible scream that can kill those who hear it. Choose up to ten creatures within range. Each target with 50 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or fewer dies. Targets with more than 50 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes {@damage 12d10} Psychic damage and has the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition for 1 hour. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only. A target is unaffected by the spell if it can't hear you.

name: Waves of Exhaustion
text:
You evoke a nimbus of flickering gray light around your body. For the duration, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to emit a wave of gray light in a 60-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. Creatures in that area must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level. This spell can't increase a creature's {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level above 4.
{@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels gained from this spell are removed when the spell ends.

name: Wither and Bloom

components.m: a withered vine twisted into a loop

text:
You invoke both death and life in a 10-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on a point within range. Each creature of your choice in that area makes a Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 3d6} Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Nonmagical plants in that area that aren't creatures, such as trees and shrubs, wither.
In addition, one creature of your choice in that area can roll one of its unexpended {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} and regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the roll plus your spellcasting ability modifier. That die is then expended.
higher:
Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
The damage increases by {@dice 1d6} for each spell slot level above 2. The number of {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} that can be rolled and expended increases by one for each spell slot level above 2. You add your spellcasting modifier to the number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} regained by this spell only once, regardless of the number of {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} rolled and expended.

name: Zone of Amicability
text: A magical zone of amicability radiates from you in a 60-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} for the duration. When you make an ability check to influence a creature in that area, you can treat a {@dice d20} roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

name: Antagonize

components.m: a playing card depicting a rogue

text: You whisper magical words that antagonize one creature of your choice within range. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes {@damage 4d4} psychic damage and must immediately use its reaction to make a melee attack against another creature of your choice that you can see. If the target can't make this attack (for example, because there is no one within its reach or because its reaction is unavailable), the target instead has disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage only.
higher:
At Higher Levels
When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by {@scaledamage 4d4|3-9|1d4} for each slot level above 3rd.

name: Spray of Cards
text: You spray a 15-foot cone of spectral cards. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 2d10} force damage and has the {@condition blinded} condition until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.
higher:
At Higher Levels
When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by {@scaledamage 2d10|2-9|1d10} for each slot level above 2nd.
